summary: Quote latency across trading screens is a downstream symptom of an infrastructure failure at the shared redis-cache. At 13:22:10 the redis-cache primary node (redis-cache-2) failed health checks (3 consecutive PING timeouts) and was marked down; at 13:22:52 the failover controller promoted replica redis-cache-3, whose dataset was EMPTY because it was mid-resync. The empty primary collapsed the cache hit ratio from ~96% to ~16%, causing market-data-service to enter a "cache miss storm", rebuilding every quote from the exchange feed snapshot (1-8s per key). Those slow lookups propagated up into pricing-engine as "quote computation deadline exceeded", pushing pricing-engine p99 from ~60ms to ~2100ms. There is no code deployment or config change on pricing-engine, market-data-service, or redis-cache; exchange-gateway latency is flat and redis CPU/evictions are flat, ruling out dependency, capacity, and resource-exhaustion causes. The service is self-recovering as the cache re-warms (p99 falling from 2100ms toward 1170ms). Confidence in the root cause is high given a directly logged causal chain.

ranked_hypotheses.title: redis-cache primary node failure with empty-replica promotion (infrastructure failure)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The redis-cache primary (redis-cache-2) failed health checks (3 consecutive PING timeouts) and was marked down at 13:22:10; the failover controller promoted replica redis-cache-3, whose dataset was empty because it was mid-resync. The resulting cold cache collapsed hit ratio to ~16% and forced market-data-service to rebuild every quote from the exchange feed (1-8s per key), which propagated into pricing-engine as 'quote computation deadline exceeded' and elevated p99 to ~2s. Fault origin: redis-cache node/infrastructure.

causal_chain.claim: redis-cache-2 primary fails health checks (3 PING timeouts) and is marked down at 13:22:10
Failover promotes redis-cache-3, whose dataset is empty (was resyncing) at 13:22:52
Cache hit ratio collapses from ~96% to ~16%
market-data-service enters cache miss storm, rebuilding quotes from exchange feed snapshot in 1-8s
pricing-engine quote computation deadline exceeded; p99 rises to ~2100ms

assumptions: The 'MARKET DATA' rebuild path actually calls the exchange feed via the normal path (no separate fast path)
No earlier undetected replica lag issue beyond what redis logs show

ranked_hypotheses.title: Capacity saturation: market-open load overwhelmed redis/cache capacity
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Record load could have exceeded provisioned cache capacity, causing evictions and misses. Rejected: redis evictions/min stayed flat ~3/min and cpu_pct flat ~22%, request_rate to market-data-service stayed flat ~950 req/s, and memory FELL rather than rising — no saturation signature.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: No rise in evictions, CPU, request rate, or memory; the cache emptied (memory fell) which is inconsistent with load-driven saturation. Also onset is a step change at 13:22, not a gradual load ramp.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Bad deployment to market-data-service/pricing-engine
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A release could have introduced slow code. Rejected: no deployments exist for market-data-service (count 0) or pricing-engine. Rejected also because the timing of the fault traces to redis-cache failover, and past incident HIST-101 (bcrypt) is a different mechanism.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: No deployment for the implicated services; get_deployments returned count 0 for market-data-service and redis-cache. Fault coincides exactly with redis-cache failover, not a release.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Dependency failure at exchange-gateway/exchange feed
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The external exchange feed could be slow. Rejected: exchange-gateway p99 latency stayed ~127-133ms flat across the incident. The 'rebuilding from exchange feed snapshot' is triggered by cache misses, not by a slow feed.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: exchange-gateway latency was flat; the rebuild latency is from cache misses, not a degraded external provider.

facts.statement: pricing-engine p99 latency jumped from ~60ms to ~1800ms avg starting in the 13:20 bucket and is slowly recovering.
pricing-engine errors are all 'quote computation deadline exceeded: market-data-service took <n>ms' (192 occurrences, up to 8456ms).
redis-cache primary node redis-cache-2 was marked down at 13:22:10 after 3 consecutive PING timeouts.
Failover at 13:22:52 promoted replica redis-cache-3 whose dataset was empty (replica was resyncing).
redis-cache hit ratio collapsed from ~96% to ~16% during the incident and is recovering.
market-data-service logged a cache miss storm rebuilding quotes from the exchange feed snapshot in 1-8s, starting 13:22:25.
market-data-service p99 latency jumped from ~39ms to ~1536ms in the 13:20 bucket.
exchange-gateway p99 stayed flat ~130ms throughout, ruling out the external feed as the slow component.
redis-cache CPU (~22%) and evictions (~3/min) stayed flat, ruling out CPU/eviction saturation.
redis-cache memory dropped from ~70% to ~9% (datastore emptied), consistent with an empty promoted replica rather than memory pressure.
No deployments exist for market-data-service or redis-cache; only an unrelated auth-service v7.2.0 deploy at 11:30.
No configuration or feature-flag changes were recorded for any service in the window.
redis-cache saw client reconnect storms post-failover (15048 and 92851 new connections in 10s).

assumptions: The redis-cache failover decision and replica resync state are genuine and not an artifact of the logging pipeline (logs are internally consistent with the metric collapse).
market-data-service rebuilds directly from the exchange feed snapshot on a cache miss, so any cold cache causes the observed 1-8s rebuilds.
No config change to redis-cache occurred (get_config_changes returned empty), so the primary failure was not caused by a configuration edit.
get_deployments for all services was partial, but the implicated services (market-data-service, redis-cache) returned full count-0 results, so absence of deploys there is reliable.

timeline.event: Unrelated auth-service v7.2.0 deploy (session cookie hardening) — not temporally linked to onset.
Last healthy bucket: pricing-engine p99 ~60ms, market-data-service p99 ~40ms, redis hit ratio ~95.8%.
redis-cache-2 primary fails health check (3 consecutive PING timeouts) and is marked down.
market-data-service begins logging 'cache miss storm ... not in redis-cache, rebuilding from exchange feed snapshot'.
Failover promotes replica redis-cache-3, whose dataset is empty (was resyncing).
pricing-engine begins logging 'quote computation deadline exceeded: market-data-service took 5171ms'.
redis-cache client reconnect storm (15048 new connections in 10s); 92851 at 13:40:15.
Incident reported (SEV-2); pricing-engine p99 ~2124ms, hit ratio trough ~16%.
Partial recovery: pricing-engine p99 down to ~1172ms, redis hit ratio back to ~46%.

recommended_actions.action: Warm/repopulate the redis-cache quotes keyspace (or trigger market-data-service to re-prime the cache) to accelerate recovery of hit ratio and quote latency.
recommended_actions.rationale: The system is recovering only as the cache re-warms (hit ratio 16% -> 46%); forcing a warm-up will cut time-to-recovery.

recommended_actions.action: Investigate why redis-cache-2 (primary) failed health checks / became unreachable (host, network, or process) — inspect node-level and infra metrics.
recommended_actions.rationale: The trigger is the primary node losing PING responses; without finding why, it may recur.

recommended_actions.action: Fix the replication/failover configuration so promotion never selects an unsynced/empty replica (e.g. min-replicas-to-write, replica-serve-stale-data, or block promotion when replica sync is incomplete).
recommended_actions.rationale: The empty promoted replica is what turned a node blip into a full cold-cache outage; preventing it removes the amplification.

recommended_actions.action: Add alerting on redis-cache cache hit ratio and replica sync state so an empty-primary condition is detected immediately.
recommended_actions.rationale: Hit ratio collapse was the direct driver of the miss storm but there was no early signal before customer-visible latency.

recommended_actions.action: Implement negative-cache / request coalescing for quote lookups in market-data-service to cap rebuild fan-out during a cold cache.
recommended_actions.rationale: Every miss triggers a 1-8s exchange-feed rebuild; coalescing would bound the impact of any future cold cache.

recommended_actions.action: Add replica-sync health checks before failover (prevent promotion of resyncing replicas) — mirrors HIST-107 resolution.
recommended_actions.rationale: HIST-107 (Cold cache storm after redis failover) had the same empty-replica root cause; the prior fix was not applied here.

data_gaps: Node/infrastructure telemetry for redis-cache-2 (the failed primary) is not available — the root trigger of its PING timeouts (host failure, network partition, OOM kill, process crash) cannot be confirmed.
get_deployments for all services was marked partial (one backend shard did not respond), though per-service queries for market-data-service and redis-cache returned complete count-0 results.
The full set of redis-cache logs is truncated (35 matched, 20 returned); additional failure-mode log lines (e.g. OOM, connection errors) may exist beyond those retrieved.
No metric directly showing redis-cache replica replication lag/offset before 13:22 — only the failover log line states the replica was resyncing.

pricing-engine ERRORs are all of the form 'quote computation deadline exceeded: market-data-service took <n>ms', first seen 13:23:57 with values from 827ms up to 8456ms; 192 such errors.

findings.statement: market-data-service p99 latency was flat ~39ms until 13:10, then jumped in the 13:20 bucket to avg 1535.72ms (max 1979.98ms), tracking the pricing-engine degradation.

exchange-gateway p99 latency stayed flat at ~127-133ms across the entire window including the incident period (e.g. 13:20 avg 132.17, 13:30 avg 131.23), so the upstream exchange feed itself was not slow.
redis-cache cpu_pct stayed flat ~22% through the incident (13:20 avg 21.85, 13:30 avg 21.68) and evictions_per_min stayed flat ~3/min (13:20 avg 2.91, 13:30 avg 3.03).

redis-cache memory_pct FELL during the incident rather than rising: 70.34% at 13:00, down to avg 9.32% at 13:30, i.e. the datastore emptied out (consistent with an empty promoted replica, not memory pressure).

The only deployment across all services in the window is auth-service v7.2.0 ('Session cookie hardening') at 11:30:00Z; no deployments exist for market-data-service or redis-cache (count 0 each), and the listing was marked partial.
No configuration or feature-flag changes were recorded for any service, including redis-cache, in the window (count 0, scope all services and redis-cache).
redis-cache logged client reconnect storms after the failover: 15048 new connections in 10s at 13:30:20 and 92851 at 13:40:15, indicating clients thundering back to the new primary.

refs.quote: client reconnect storm: 15048 new connections in 10s

findings.statement: The failure originated in redis-cache infrastructure (primary node health-check failure forcing promotion of an unsynced/empty replica), not in pricing-engine or market-data-service; those services only reflected the resulting cache-miss latency.
